summary: New hires intermittently get 403 at Feature Flag Editor due to Okta claim mapping change
description: Issue summary: Several new hires and contractors report successful Okta SSO but receive 403 when opening the Feature Flag Editor or Model Observability dashboards. Impact: prevents feature flag edits and internal investigations for affected users. Environment: production (identity proxy + console); reports primarily from us-west and eu-west. Symptoms: Okta SAML/OIDC assertion completes, user can see the console shell, but API requests to /api/feature-flags and /api/model-observability return 403 with logs showing 'rbac: missing affiliation claim'. Steps to reproduce: 1) New user completes Okta onboarding and signs in. 2) Click 'Feature Flag Editor' or 'Model Observability'. 3) Console UI loads but API calls fail with 403. Observed logs: identity-proxy: "WARN claim_transformer: expected 'affiliation' claim not found for subject=svc_user_abc"; console-auth: "ERROR rbac: role lookup failed: no roles derived from claims for uid=U12345". Temporary workaround: manual group assignment in internal admin console grants access; rolling back recent Okta claim-transformer change also restores access for repro users. Notes: this appears correlated with yesterday's Okta expression update that migrated several customer-facing apps to the new 'employmentAffiliation' attribute name.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: okta-claim-transformer renamed claim without updating downstream RBAC consumers, causing role derivation to fail.
Identity-proxy logs show raw assertion payloads missing 'affiliation' for affected users; Okta Admin audit shows expression update deployed 2026-03-11 22:03 UTC (slack #identity-change thread).
Trace: user U12345 -> okta -> identity-proxy -> issued token missing 'affiliation' -> console-auth returned 403. Correlation across ~12 incidents within 3 hours after deployment.
Risk assessment: P1 because it prevents new hires and contractors from performing triage and feature flag changes; existing users with cached roles mostly unaffected.
Repro run: Reproduced by creating test account with onboarding flow; after rollback to claim-transformer v2.1.3 user gets 'affiliation' claim and access is normal.
Related: similar symptom to INT-271919 where claim normalization caused runbook access problems; reuse follow-up checklist from that ticket.
resolution_notes: Action taken: Rolled out patch to identity-proxy and console-auth to accept both 'affiliation' and 'employmentAffiliation' claim keys. Canary completed and progressive rollout finished 2026-03-14 11:30 UTC.
Workaround used: Manual internal admin group assignment for affected users while fix was deployed. Identity team rolled back the Okta expression for internal app overnight to reduce blast radius.
Permanent fix: Merge PR-842 (identity) and PR-1293 (console) to normalize claim handling and add a deprecation notice for 'affiliation'. Updated claim-transformer documentation.

Follow-ups: 1) Create end-to-end integration test ensuring role derivation succeeds when either claim key is present (owner: Console Eng, due 2026-03-21). 2) Add monitoring alert for 'rbac: missing affiliation' spikes (owner: SRE, due 2026-03-18). 3) Add a one-week rollout monitor and send usage report to security and onboarding teams.
Status: Functional fix deployed and verified. Ticket remains open for postmortem and follow-ups.
